—(1) Where the court considers an application under rule 77.23(1) it may—] (a)gives the required undertaking under paragraph (3), the claimant must, within two days of the date on which it is served on them—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.25. —(1) Where the court considers an application under rule 77.23(1) it may—] (i)serve on the legal representative the relevant material in full or as directed; or

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.25. —(1) Where the court considers an application under rule 77.23(1) it may—] (ii)inform both the court and the defendant of their decision not to rely on it; or

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.25. —(1) Where the court considers an application under rule 77.23(1) it may—] (b)does not give the required undertaking within the time specified in paragraph (3) or informs the court of their decision not to give undertakings, the claimant must seek further directions from the court. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.25. —(1) Where the court considers an application under rule 77.23(1) it may—] (5) Where the court does not give permission to withhold relevant material from the defendant, or has made a direction under rule 77.23(2)(c), within seven days after the date on which they are notified of the court’s decision or such other period as the court may direct, the claimant must—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.25. —(1) Where the court considers an application under rule 77.23(1) it may—] (a)serve on the defendant the relevant material in full, or as directed; or

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.25. —(1) Where the court considers an application under rule 77.23(1) it may—] (b)inform both the court and the defendant of their decision not to rely on it. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.25. —(1) Where the court considers an application under rule 77.23(1) it may—] (6) Where the claimant has informed the court of their decision not to rely on the relevant material in full or as directed—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.25. —(1) Where the court considers an application under rule 77.23(1) it may—] (a)the claimant shall not be required to serve the relevant material on the defendant or comply with the direction; but

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.25. —(1) Where the court considers an application under rule 77.23(1) it may—] (b)the court may, at a hearing on notice, if it considers that the relevant material or anything that is required to be summarised or redacted might adversely affect the claimant’s case or support the case of the defendant, direct that the claimant is not to rely on such points, or that the claimant makes such concessions or takes such other steps, as the court may direct. ## Hearings

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Hearings] 77.26. —(1) Where the court considers it necessary to exclude the defendant from any hearing or part of that hearing to ensure that relevant material subject to a direction under rule 77.23(2) is not disclosed to them, the court must direct that the hearing, or that part of it from which the defendant is excluded, be conducted in private. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Hearings] (2) Unless the court directs otherwise, the court shall serve notice of the date, time and place fixed for a hearing on every party and, if one has been appointed for the purposes of the proceedings, the special advocate or those instructing the special advocate. ## Special advocates

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates] 77.27. —(1) In any proceedings to which this Sub-section applies, the court may at any stage direct the claimant to request the Attorney General to appoint a special advocate to represent the interests of the defendant. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates] (2) The function of a special advocate is to represent the interests of the defendant by, for example—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates] (a)making submissions to the court at any hearing from which the party and that party’s legal representative are excluded;

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates] (b)adducing evidence and cross-examining witnesses at such a hearing;

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates] (c)making applications to the court or seeking directions from the court where necessary; and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates] (d)making written submissions to the court, including whether relevant material withheld under rule 77.23(2) should be disclosed in full or in a summary or redacted version. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates] (3) Where the court makes a direction under paragraph (1), the claimant—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates] (a)must within seven days of receipt of notification of their appointment, serve on the special advocate, copies of—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates] (i)the claim form and further material specified in rule 77.19(2), and any further evidence served on the defendant;

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates] (ii)the acknowledgement of service and any further evidence served by the defendant;

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates] (iii)the application under rule 77.23(1) and the relevant material and documents specified in rule 77.24(1); and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates] (iv)if applicable, the court’s direction under rule 77.23(2); and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates] (b)may not rely on the relevant material which is the subject of the application under rule 77.23(1) unless a special advocate has been appointed, and the relevant material has been served on them. ## Special advocates – communicating about proceedings

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates – communicating about proceedings] 77.28. —(1) A special advocate may communicate with the defendant, or their legal representative, at any time before the claimant serves the relevant material on the special advocate. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates – communicating about proceedings] (2) After the relevant material has been served on the special advocate, they must not communicate with any person about any matter connected with the proceedings, except in accordance with paragraphs (3), (4) or (8)(b) or with a direction of the court pursuant to a request under paragraph (5). [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates – communicating about proceedings] (3) The special advocate may, without directions from the court, communicate about the proceedings with—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates – communicating about proceedings] (a)the court;

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates – communicating about proceedings] (b)the claimant;

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates – communicating about proceedings] (c)the Attorney General and any persons acting for the Attorney General;

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates – communicating about proceedings] (d)any other person, except for the defendant or their legal representative, with whom it is necessary for administrative purposes for the special advocate to communicate about matters not connected with the substance of the proceedings. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates – communicating about proceedings] (4) The special advocate may communicate with the defendant or their legal representative with the express agreement of the claimant. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates – communicating about proceedings] (5) The special advocate may request directions from the court authorising them to communicate with—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates – communicating about proceedings] (a)subject to paragraph (6), the defendant or their legal representative; or

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates – communicating about proceedings] (b)with any other person. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates – communicating about proceedings] (6) Where the special advocate wishes to communicate with the defendant or their legal representative, the special advocate may not, without good reason, request directions under paragraph (5)(a) unless the claimant has refused their request under paragraph (4). [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates – communicating about proceedings] (7) Where the special advocate requests directions under paragraph (5)—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates – communicating about proceedings] (a)the special advocate must notify the claimant of the request; and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates – communicating about proceedings] (b)the claimant must, within two days or such other period as may be directed by the court, file and serve on the special advocate notice of any objection to the proposed communication, or to the form in which it is proposed to be made. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates – communicating about proceedings] (8) Paragraph (2) does not prohibit the defendant or their legal representative communicating with the special advocate after the claimant has served relevant material on the special advocate, but—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates – communicating about proceedings] (a)they may only do so in writing; and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Special advocates – communicating about proceedings] (b)the special advocate must not reply to the communication other than in accordance with directions given by the court, except that the special advocate may, under paragraph (4) or without such directions, send a written acknowledgment of receipt. ## Consideration of the claimant’s objection under rule 77.28(7)(b)

## 77.29. —(1) If the claimant objects to a proposed communication under rule 77.28(7)(b)—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.29. —(1) If the claimant objects to a proposed communication under rule 77.28(7)(b)—] (a)the special advocate may file and serve on the claimant a reply to the objection;

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.29. —(1) If the claimant objects to a proposed communication under rule 77.28(7)(b)—] (b)the claimant and the special advocate must file with the court a schedule identifying the issues which cannot be agreed between them and which must—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.29. —(1) If the claimant objects to a proposed communication under rule 77.28(7)(b)—] (i)give brief reasons for their contentions on each issue in dispute; and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.29. —(1) If the claimant objects to a proposed communication under rule 77.28(7)(b)—] (ii)set out any proposals for the court to resolve the issues in dispute. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.29. —(1) If the claimant objects to a proposed communication under rule 77.28(7)(b)—] (2) On receipt of the claimant’s objection, the special advocate may give notice that they do not challenge it. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.29. —(1) If the claimant objects to a proposed communication under rule 77.28(7)(b)—] (3) The court may—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.29. —(1) If the claimant objects to a proposed communication under rule 77.28(7)(b)—] (a)consider the claimant’s objection without a hearing; or

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.29. —(1) If the claimant objects to a proposed communication under rule 77.28(7)(b)—] (b)if the court considers that it is necessary before it can determine the matter, direct a hearing. ## Failure to comply with directions

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Failure to comply with directions] 77.30. —(1) Where the claimant or special advocate fails to comply with a direction of the court, the court may serve on the claimant or the special advocate a notice which states—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Failure to comply with directions] (a)the respect in which they have failed to comply with the direction;

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Failure to comply with directions] (b)a time limit for complying with the direction; and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Failure to comply with directions] (c)that the court may proceed to determine the proceedings before it, on the material available to it, if they fail to comply with the relevant direction within the time specified. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Failure to comply with directions] (2) Where the claimant or special advocate fails to comply with such a notice, the court may proceed in accordance with paragraph (1)(c). ## Orders under the 1997 Act and 2003 Act

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Orders under the 1997 Act and 2003 Act] 77.31. —(1) Where the court makes an order in any proceedings to which this Sub-section applies, it may withhold any, or any part, of its reasons if and to the extent that it is not possible to give those reasons without disclosing material, the disclosure of which would adversely affect—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Orders under the 1997 Act and 2003 Act] (a)the prevention of disorder or crime; or

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Orders under the 1997 Act and 2003 Act] (b)the health or welfare of the defendant or any other person. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Orders under the 1997 Act and 2003 Act] (2) Where the court’s judgment does not include the full reasons for its decision, the court must serve on the claimant, the defendant’s legal representative if appropriate, and, if appointed, the special advocate, a separate written judgment giving those reasons. ## Supply of court documents

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > Supply of court documents] 77.32. Unless the court otherwise directs, rule 5.4B (supply of documents from court records – a party) and rule 5.4C (supply of court documents – a non-party) do not apply to any proceedings to which this Sub-section applies. ## Appeals

## 77.33. —(1) Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.33. —(1) Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal—] (a)against an order of the High Court on or in relation to an application under rule 77.23(1); and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.33. —(1) Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal—] (b)where the order under appeal was not made on or in relation to a matter within sub-paragraph (a) but the appeal proceedings involve such a matter. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.33. —(1) Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal—] (2) Paragraph (1) is subject to—

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.33. —(1) Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal—] (a)this Sub-section; and

[PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.33. —(1) Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal—] (b)paragraph (3) of this rule. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.33. —(1) Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal—] (3) The appellant must serve a copy of the appellant’s notice on any special advocate. [PART 77 – PROVISIONS IN SUPPORT OF CRIMINAL JUSTICE > 77.33. —(1) Part 52 (appeals) applies to an appeal to the Court of Appeal—] (4) Unless the court directs otherwise, an appeal to the Court of Appeal in proceedings under paragraph (1), must be determined at a hearing. ## Footnotes
